findings.reason: without adding `tests/test_brief_prompt.py` to the write paths and naming the snapshot update as part of the deliverable, the node cannot satisfy its own done-when and its gate is unpassable as written.
findings.text: §6's done-when names `tests/test_brief_prompt.py` among the suites that must pass at the head, but that file asserts `_compose() == PLAN_PROMPT_SNAPSHOT`, a byte-identical literal of the composed prompt (`tests/test_brief_prompt.py:241`, snapshot at `:249-424`), whose lines 316-322 reproduce `CONTRACT — WHO CLOSES THE NODE` verbatim; rewording `CLOSURE_AUTHORITY_CONTRACT` therefore reddens that test, and `tests/test_brief_prompt.py` is not in §6's write-path list (`reckon/crew/prompts.py`, the three skill files, `tests/test_crew_prompts.py`, `tests/test_skill_contract_parity.py`), so a worker obeying the scope either leaves a failing suite or edits a file its fence withholds

findings.reason: naming which literals move (the snapshot in `test_brief_prompt.py`, and `CLOSURE_NO_SELF_CLOSE`/`CLOSURE_TERMINAL_LIMIT` in `test_crew_prompts.py`) is what stops the worker from discovering the coupling mid-node, where a mismatch reads as a defect in the reword rather than in the fixtures.
findings.text: the same literal makes the section's "passes at the head" clause read as a property of the change rather than of the snapshot: `tests/test_crew_prompts.py` also pins the exact word "does not close its own node" (`CLOSURE_NO_SELF_CLOSE`, `tests/test_crew_prompts.py:361`), so a reword that follows the deliverable's "names what the worker may not close" phrasing but drops that clause fails a file that IS in scope and that §6 does not say to update

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `CLOSURE_AUTHORITY_CONTRACT` is at `reckon/crew/prompts.py:248`, the quoted "must not set a terminal status" at `:251`, the MANIFEST status vocabulary at `:896`, `can_land` at `:751 and :775`, the three skill mirrors at `skills/reckon-build/SKILL.md:435`, `skills/reckon-build/references/sprint-orchestration.md:519`, `skills/reckon-build/references/coordinator-reference.md:805`, `LIMIT_SKILL_FILES` at `tests/test_skill_contract_parity.py:128`, and both cited runs exist under `~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/`; `crew check --manifest` refuses a status outside `complete/blocked/failed` at `reckon/crew/reports.py:2579`. The "near lines 756 and 775" pointer lands 756 inside the composition's explanatory comment and 775 on the assignment that gates the block — near enough, and `can_land` is computed at 751.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §6's done-when requires `tests/test_brief_prompt.py` to pass at the head, but that file embeds a byte-identical literal of the composed prompt and is not among §6's declared write paths (`plan.html:83`).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §6 names the test files and the message-level evidence (run ids, command output) it relies on; no gate log is placed in a scratch or node-local path, and the run manifest carries the gate logs under the crew run directory.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §6 introduces no symbol, file or comment carrying a plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag; its section names are plan-internal HTML, not source.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the root cause matches the cited evidence, and the mechanism (reword `CLOSURE_AUTHORITY_CONTRACT`, mirror into the three skill files, add `coordinator-reference.md` to `LIMIT_SKILL_FILES`) reaches the real code path (`compose_prompt`), but the mechanism cannot produce the done-when because one test the done-when names reproduces the prompt verbatim and is outside §6's write paths.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §6 names one deliverable: the closure contract stops reading as a ban on the manifest status, with its three mirrors and the two tests that measure it; the mirrors and the test-list addition are the same change, not a second goal.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §6's ordering claim is carried by the plan's own data: `plan-section-depends-on` at `plan.html:24` declares `s3` waiting on `the-crew-contract-fits-one-read#s6`, and §6's text states it runs before §3.
